source_title: Delhi Mock Parliament: Opposition Leaders' Seats Set, Will BJP's Top Leadership Join the Debate?
source_excerpt:
New Delhi is set to witness a unique political exercise as Citizen for Democracy organises a mock Parliament at the NDMC Convention Centre under the theme 'Democracy vs Anarchy'. The event aims to recreate the atmosphere of the Lok Sabha, with separate seating arrangements and nameplates for prominent leaders from both the ruling alliance and the opposition. The mock Parliament comes amid continuing political disagreements over the functioning of constitutional institutions and allegations raised by opposition leaders against key constitutional authorities. Issues involving the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Chief Election Commissioner and other constitutional institutions are expected to form the backdrop of the discussion. The venue has been arranged to resemble the actual Parliament, with nameplates bearing the names of Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Akhilesh Yadav placed on the opposition side. On the other side, seats have been marked for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, Nitin Nabin, Anurag Thakur and other prominent NDA leaders. According to the information shared from the venue, researchers, scholars, legal experts and other participants are expected to take part in the exercise. The organisers are attempting to create a parliamentary-style setting where the ongoing political debate surrounding democracy, constitutional institutions and allegations of institutional interference can be discussed. However, an important question remains over the participation of senior BJP leaders. According to reporter Pawan Gaur's update, no prominent BJP leader is expected to attend the programme so far. The event is being organised by Citizen for Democracy, and the participation of political representatives remains a key point of interest. The mock Parliament is expected to bring the country's ongoing political debate into a simulated parliamentary setting, drawing attention to the contrasting positions of the ruling alliance and opposition.
